description: The image displays three pie charts from the R2I-Bench benchmark, which evaluates reasoning-driven text-to-image generation, each illustrating the distribution of different logical or semantic categories. The first chart, labeled “Categorical,” is divided into four segments: “Limiter” (27.91%, light pink), “Universal Quantifiers” (29.07%, light blue), “Negation” (27.91%, orange), and “Existential Quantifiers” (15.12%, light green), with the largest segment being Universal Quantifiers. The second chart, with a blurred title, contains three segments: “Approximate Quantities” (45.03%, beige), “Comparative Relationships” (36.26%, light blue), and “Absolute Absence” (18.71%, lavender), showing that approximate quantities dominate this category. The third chart, titled “Disjunctive & Conjunctive,” is nearly evenly split into two segments: “Conjunctive” (50.49%, light purple) and “Disjunctive” (49.51%, light blue-gray), indicating a near-equal distribution between conjunctive and disjunctive reasoning types. Each chart uses distinct colors and includes percentage labels within the slices for clarity.
